criteria.notes: Actual decaying restricted-coordinate S modules are constructed, with finite-support polynomial truncations and coordinatewise recovery from every compatible quotient record. Both inverse identities, choice independence and S-linearity are verified, for A and B. Derives the actual finite quotients of C, then both inverse coordinate-record maps for the decaying truncated-power-series model. The coordinate at max(nu_n,1) correctly includes nu_n=0. All finite-support and compatibility conditions are proved. Writes the actual diagonal multiplication and coordinate reduction and proves they coincide with the original induced maps in each quotient. The preliminary argument defines the S action and verifies functorial S-linearity. The actual projection from Chat onto C/t^m C is surjective and its kernel is proved equal to t^m Chat by the normalized polynomial lift and uniform division in the decaying B model. The compatible quotient isomorphisms identify eta_Chat with the inverse of their limit, rather than presuming idempotence.

Proves diagonal injectivity by cancellation in S, identifies the kernel K by actual coordinate divisibility, and defines the image I using preimages still satisfying the unweighted decay requirement. These are explicitly submodules of the completed B model, not confused with the whole product or each other. The normalized coordinate representatives are proved to give a genuine decaying lift for every Chat element in 1.3. Section1.4 describes every fiber as its translate of the full kernel, with the correct weighted-decay condition; section2.4 proves the induced p is onto. Proves the actual power-submodule identity for completed B. Both closure inclusions then follow: each coordinate divisibility condition is detected at its finite exponent, and the finite exceptional low-order coordinates produce an element of I agreeing modulo t^m. Thus the stated closure is for the actual t-adic topology. Classifies exactness for every exponent sequence. A common finite upper bound preserves decay under coordinatewise division; any unbounded sequence admits increasing indices with nu_n at least their index, giving an actual kernel element whose unique preimage has infinitely many constant coordinates. No monotonicity or whole-sequence divergence is added.

Defines the weighted-decaying module Ktilde and proves diagonal multiplication is an S-module isomorphism onto K, taking the unweighted module onto I. It therefore identifies E with Ktilde/M_A. Section2.4 binds E=0 precisely to the already-proved bounded-exponent classification. Section2.2 proves j well-defined and injective, its exact finite-support image, its S-submodule/direct-sum identity, the optional floor-coordinate description, and its zero intersection with E. Section2.3 proves both torsion inclusions: t^r b=Da permits division outside the finite exceptional support and subtraction of Dd, leaving a finite-support representative. Gives two valid proofs of E torsion freeness. The direct model uniformly removes a fixed power of t from decay and uses the unit factor of every nonzero scalar; the second proof uses the established intersection of E with j(C). For bounded exponents p itself is an isomorphism. For every unbounded sequence constructs an actual infinite-support, decaying, nonzero t-killed element of Chat. An S-linear section would lift it to the classified torsion subgroup j(C), whose image has finite support, a contradiction.

Proves the actual maps induced by p are onto, identifies their kernel as (E+t^m Q)/t^m Q, and makes this zero using the independently proved image closure. Section3.3 takes the compatible inverse limit, identifying phat and the precise relation beta eta_Q=p. The image-closure argument gives E contained in every t^m Q; the reverse inclusion follows from Chat separatedness. Section3.3 identifies eta_Q as an actual surjection with kernel E, hence an isomorphism exactly when the exponents are bounded by section2.4. Proves an explicit description of L_m=t^m Ktilde+M_A as the sequences with finite low-order exception set. Their intersection is exactly M_A, proving separatedness. For any compatible record, subtracts the successive M_A errors, obtains coordinatewise increments t^m y^(m), and constructs a weighted-decaying limit using uniform divisibility. This limit represents every original quotient record, proving actual canonical completeness without an unjustified general quotient-completeness assertion. Separates the two filtrations: E intersection t^m Q is E, giving the indiscrete inherited topology, whereas the intrinsic topology is separated by the preceding complete coordinate proof. Equality forces E=t^m E for every m and therefore E=0, equivalent to bounded exponents. The zero-module boundary is explicitly handled.

All independent extras are correct: eta is S-linear for an S module; j has the stated S-submodule/direct-sum and floor-coordinate descriptions; E intersects j(C) trivially; the completion of E->Q is zero; and when E is nonzero its intrinsic power-submodule chain is strictly descending by torsion-free cancellation and separatedness. The source word for indiscrete topology is read with its explicit set of opens, including its separately handled singleton case. No unsupported extra theorem or alternative core assumption is introduced.
